clue.text: Colour gets base coat about right; with eggshell initially, to paint afresh?

parts.note: red is a colour
e is the base of natural logarithms in maths

indicators.note: about means going round, so the coat wraps around the next piece
initially means only the opening letter of eggshell is used

explanation.surface: A decorator's instructions: colour, base coat and eggshell finish for repainting a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside COAT to make CORAT; E for 'base' is the mathematical constant. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To redecorate a room is to give it a fresh coat of paint or new furnishings.

clue.text: German region's visitor hurried up somewhat

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
somewhat says only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A tourist in Germany hurried up a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes RHUR from visitoR HURried; 'up' turns it round. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr is the industrial area of western Germany around Essen and Dortmund.

clue.text: Trashed second old city during performance

indicators.note: during says the earlier pieces sit inside the performance

parts.note: a deed is something performed, an act
Troy is the ancient city of the Trojan War

explanation.surface: An ancient city was wrecked in the course of a theatrical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' suggests a show, but here it is an act or feat; 'during' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trashed has been wrecked or ruined, the same as destroyed.

clue.text: Irish food that's a winner!

definitions.meaning: an Irish dish of mashed potato with spring onions

explanation.surface: Praise for a favourite Irish dish as the best of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Champ is both mashed potato with scallions and an informal word for a champion.

clue.text: People taking things the wrong way?

definitions.text: People taking things the wrong way?

parts.words: People taking things the wrong way?
parts.note: taking something the wrong way usually means misunderstanding it, but here it means taking it illegally

explanation.surface: People who misunderstand what is said to them.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'take the wrong way' suggests offence; read literally it is taking by wrongful means: theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves take property by unlawful means, a wrongful way of acquiring things.

clue.text: The northern ducks walk like this? That's nonsense!

parts.note: in northern English dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
ducks waddle, walking with a rolling gait

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that northern ducks walk in a particular style.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire and other northern English speech 'the' is clipped to t'. 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly or empty talk, a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: A long time in stage school

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone spent many years at a theatre school.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Ages' is an informal way of saying a very long period.

clue.text: Some picking raspberries take hold eagerly

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fruit pickers eagerly grab at the berries.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp is to seize something firmly and keenly.

clue.text: Get cosy with feathers from a Yorkshire town?

indicators.note: from says the feathers come after the town, as if originating there

parts.note: Settle is a market town in North Yorkshire
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Snuggling under a quilt filled with feathers from a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a small market town in the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle down is to make oneself comfortable and relaxed.

clue.text: A female, good at speaking, that's pretty well off

parts.note: a fluent speaker talks smoothly and easily

explanation.surface: An articulate woman who is also rather wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent people have plenty of money, being comfortably wealthy.

clue.text: Landlord given a garden plant

parts.note: a landlord of a pub is the host

explanation.surface: A pub landlord receives a plant as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostas are leafy perennials grown widely in shady garden beds.

clue.text: Party where one could get one's finger on the pulse?

definitions.text: Party where one could get one's finger on the pulse?

parts.words: Party where one could get one's finger on the pulse?
parts.note: pulses are edible seeds like beans, so a feast of them lets one literally touch a pulse

explanation.surface: A gathering where one could keep up with the latest trends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finger on the pulse' means being up to date, but pulses are also beans and lentils.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast is a jolly celebration or party, originally an employer's annual dinner.

clue.text: If dressed to kill, is one this gorgeous?

definitions.text: If dressed to kill, is one this gorgeous?

parts.words: If dressed to kill, is one this gorgeous?
parts.note: dressing to kill suggests killing, and the phrase for stunning looks contains a word for being killed

explanation.surface: A question about whether dressing up glamorously makes someone stunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed to kill' means very smartly dressed; the stock phrase for stunning beauty fits the killing idea too.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop-dead is an informal intensifier for strikingly attractive, as in drop-dead gorgeous.

clue.text: Part of jacket friend returned, with middle of belt

indicators.note: returned means the word for friend is read backwards

parts.note: pal is an informal word for friend

indicators.note: middle of means the central letters of belt are taken

explanation.surface: A friend gave back part of a jacket along with a belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns PAL into LAP; 'middle of' takes EL from bELt.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded flap on the front of a coat or jacket.

clue.text: Pugnacious, troubled Sis with 'veg rage'!

indicators.note: troubled suggests disturbance, so the letters of these words are shaken up

explanation.surface: A sister upset and furious in a fit of anger about vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges SISVEGRAGE. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pugnacious is eager to fight, which is what aggressive describes.

clue.text: Old blokes heard: they spout a lot!

indicators.note: heard says the word for old blokes is said out loud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: geezers is slang for men, especially old ones

explanation.surface: Old men overheard, who talk endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they spout a lot' suggests garrulous old men; it is the hot springs.
explanation.definitionFit: Geysers are springs that shoot jets of hot water into the air.

clue.text: Person who praises EU record first

parts.note: the European Union, as written
a log is a written record
1st, with the 1 read as I, gives IST

explanation.surface: Someone who speaks well of the European Union's track record above all.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogist speaks in high commendation of someone, often at a funeral.

clue.text: Dear me: excited about large gemstone

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
excited suggests agitation, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in excitement over a big jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges DEARME to EMERAD; 'about' wraps it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a precious green stone, a variety of beryl.

clue.text: One's tricked poor if all working

indicators.note: working suggests something being worked over and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor person is cheated when everyone else is employed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges POORIFALL. 'One's tricked' means one who is tricked.
explanation.definitionFit: An April fool is the victim of a prank played on the first of April.

clue.text: Spreads throughout: like some clues?

definitions.meaning: to riddle something is to permeate it, as in riddled with errors
puzzling questions, as some crossword clues are

explanation.surface: Something that permeates everything, as puzzling as a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddle means both to fill thoroughly and a puzzling question needing ingenuity.

clue.text: A diner's ordered fish

indicators.note: ordered suggests arranging, so the letters are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer has requested fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' reads as a menu choice but rearranges ADINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardine is a small oily sea fish, a young pilchard.

clue.text: Two care desperately and admit defeat

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild flailing, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A pair, each anxious, finally concede.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' rearranges TWOCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat crow is an idiom for humbly accepting one has been wrong.

clue.text: Almost finish plums seen in reserves

indicators.note: Almost means the word for finish loses its final letter

parts.note: end means finish
gages are plums, as in greengages

explanation.surface: Plums nearly ready are found stored away in supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims END to EN. 'seen in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage something, such as a room or service, is to book it in advance.

clue.text: Express indifference in Welsh rugby

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Showing a lack of interest in the game as played in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising one's shoulders shows one does not care, the gesture of unconcern.

clue.text: Fit sails etc on one end of yard that's stiff

parts.note: to rig a ship is to fit it with sails and ropes
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of yard is taken

explanation.surface: Rigging a ship with sails on a yardarm that won't bend.
explanation.walkthrough: A yard is also the spar sails hang from, keeping the nautical picture. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid things are inflexible and cannot bend.

clue.text: Lars, with gold, recreated toys

indicators.note: recreated means made again in a new form, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A man named Lars remakes playthings with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreated' rearranges LARSGOLD. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag dolls are soft children's playthings made of cloth.

clue.text: Soon, I only can hold a bulb

indicators.note: can hold says the following words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone will soon be able to grasp a light bulb, alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion grows as a layered bulb underground, used as a vegetable.

clue.text: See European agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of something, an old word for spotting.

clue.text: Eating with Scandinavian girl and rock star?

parts.note: Inge is a common Scandinavian girl's name
Sting is the singer, former frontman of The Police

explanation.surface: Having dinner with a Nordic woman and a famous musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingesting means taking food into the body, swallowing it.

clue.text: Actor Jeremy perhaps, in clubs?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a famous actor is a member of some clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Irons is an Oscar-winning actor, and irons are a set of golf clubs.

clue.text: Chap in a whirl?

definitions.meaning: A man's name, so stands for a chap
a small whirlpool or swirl of water

explanation.definitionFit: Eddy is a male name, and an eddy is a circular current in water or air.

clue.text: Salt given to friend at certain times

parts.note: to salt food is to season it
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Salt is passed to a companion now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done seasonally happens at particular periods of the year.
